task.title: Define overflow-safe fixed-interval schedule arithmetic
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/853 by establishing deterministic positive fixed-millisecond intervals and checked one-step advancement before persisting recurrence.
acceptance_criteria: Preserve every positive interval exactly and reject zero with a typed error.
Advance one caller-owned instant with checked addition, including exact u64::MAX success, and preserve both operands on overflow.
Document that arithmetic reads no clock and grants no recurrence, lifecycle, dispatch, retry, or worker authority.

attempts.diagnostic: The focused kernel test failed to compile with E0432 and E0599 because ScheduleInterval and ScheduleInstant::checked_advance did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added focused tests for positive interval preservation, zero rejection, ordinary advancement, exact u64::MAX success, and typed overflow evidence.

attempts.diagnostic: Future fixed-interval recurrence needed one deterministic arithmetic rule, while wrapping, saturation, civil time, and ambient clocks would hide invalid timing or widen authority.
attempts.patch: Added ScheduleInterval, ScheduleIntervalError, ScheduleAdvanceError, and checked one-step ScheduleInstant advancement, then recorded the contract in ADR-0035 and scheduler documentation.

attempts.summary: Preserved exact-head review discipline through temporary review limits.
attempts.diagnostic: The initial CodeRabbit status was rate limited and therefore false-green despite successful Rust CI.
attempts.patch: Kept auto-merge disabled through the stated cooldown, deliberately resumed review afterward, and merged only after CodeRabbit substantively reviewed all four changed files with no actionable comments.

outcome.summary: The kernel can represent exact positive fixed-millisecond intervals and advance caller-owned instants without wrapping, saturation, persistence, or clock authority.

lessons: Define exact checked arithmetic before making a recurrence format durable.
Positive fixed milliseconds avoid zero-progress loops and defer calendar, time-zone, and parser policy.
Typed overflow evidence should preserve every rejected operand instead of wrapping or saturating.
A rate-limited green status is not review evidence; wait for substantive review of the exact head before merge.
